name: Battle of Nicopolis, Last Major Crusade Destroyed
summary: A large Western crusading force, French, Burgundian, Hungarian, and Wallachian knights, is annihilated by Sultan Bayezid I at Nicopolis on the Danube. The Western knights' disorganized charge into Turkish lines is repulsed; Bayezid's Anatolian cavalry then destroys the demoralized crusaders. Over 10,000 captives are killed or enslaved; Jean de Nevers (the Burgundian commander) is ransomed for 200,000 gold florins.

_quarry.structural_significance: Nicopolis ends the era of Franco-Burgundian crusading enthusiasm; no western European power mounts a serious anti-Ottoman land campaign for decades; the battle demonstrates the futility of heavy cavalry charges against disciplined infantry with archery support; the Burgundian nobility's capture and ransom deepens Burgundy's fiscal crisis and focuses it on consolidating its Low Countries domains rather than eastern adventure
